environment.description: Same ASP.NET Core 7.0 application deployed on Azure App Service (Linux, P1v3 tier) behind Azure Front Door Premium. The Front Door instance has a WAF policy in Prevention mode with the DefaultRuleSet 2.1 enabled. Additionally, the App Service is deployed into a VNet-integrated subnet (delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms) with an associated NSG that has a DENY ALL outbound rule for ports 80/443 to any destination except the Azure Monitor private endpoint (10.0.1.4/32). The subnet's route table forces all other traffic through an Azure Firewall instance (10.0.0.4) which has application rules permitting ONLY *.monitoring.internal and *.applicationinsights.azure.com FQDNs. The App Service has the SCM site restricted to the VNet. The Front Door WAF custom rule set includes a rule inspecting request bodies for patterns matching '<!ENTITY' and '<!DOCTYPE.*SYSTEM' with action Block (priority 1, match condition: RequestBody contains). The SRI hash on the health endpoint's monitoring script tag ensures that even if an attacker could somehow redirect the CDN response through DNS manipulation within the constrained network, the browser would reject any script whose content doesn't match sha384-oqVuAfXRKap7fdgcCY5uykM6+R9GqQ8K/uxy9rx7HNQlGYl1kPzQho1wx4JwY8wC.
